articles.title: 'No talks unless Dharmendra Pradhan resigns': CJP warns of tougher protest
articles.description: The Cockroach Janta Party continues its protest demanding Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.  They received positive responses on compensation and legal cases during recent government meetings.  However, the group states no concrete decision has been made on their primary demand.  Activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his hunger strike after receiving written assurances from the Centre.  The CJP emphasizes accountability remains the movement's central and non-negotiable demand.

articles.title: 20-yr-old army officer's son dies after car falls into open drain in south Delhi
articles.description: Tragedy struck Vasant Kunj when a 20-year-old student named Yashvendra lost his life after his car rolled into an open drain. Having just returned from the United States, he was accompanied by a woman who managed to escape unharmed. Poor road conditions, exacerbated by recent rainfall, caused the car to skid. The police later retrieved both the vehicle and Yashvendra's body from the drain.

articles.title: From selling vegetables to e-rickshaw driver: Bihar's Jhandu is now India's first CWG 2026 medallist
articles.description: Bihar's Jhandu Kumar won India's first para powerlifting medal at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, claiming bronze in Glasgow after years of struggle. A former e-rickshaw driver who overcame financial hardship and polio, he lifted 190kg to reach the podium. "I feel as if I'm flying," Jhandu said, thanking his family, coaches, TOPS and SAI for their support.

Setback for Trump: US appeals court refuses to revive $100,000 H-1B visa fee
articles.description: A federal appeals court refused to lift a ruling blocking a $100,000 H-1B visa fee. The court left in place a decision finding the fee unlawful while the government challenges it. Democratic attorneys general argued the administration created a new tax without congressional approval. A district judge agreed, ruling the fee exceeded executive branch authority. The appellate panel said the government had not shown it was likely to prevail.

articles.title: NTA launches recruitment drive for senior officials and Young Professionals after examination reforms
articles.description: The National Testing Agency has launched a major recruitment drive after examination reforms triggered by the NEET paper leak and other irregularities. The agency has dismissed 47 officials and begun hiring four General Managers and 16 Young Professionals through the UPSC Pratibha Setu portal. The appointments will strengthen assessment, cybersecurity, test centre operations and vigilance. The NTA also plans additional recruitment and new panels of subject experts and translators under the expert committee's recommendations.
